record.paper_title: Open problems in ageing science: A roadmap for biogerontology
record.original_question: In ageing science, which tissues, organs, or cell types make the largest contribution to ageing?

evidence.quote: Which tissues, organs or cell types contribute more to ageing?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
In the biology of ageing, an organism is composed of many tissues, organs, and cell types, each of which may accumulate molecular and cellular damage (e.g., senescent cells, mitochondrial dysfunction, epigenetic drift, proteostasis loss, stem-cell exhaustion) over time and may exert systemic effects on other tissues via secreted factors, immune signaling, or structural support. Define the "contribution" of a given tissue, organ, or cell type to organismal ageing as the degree to which age-related dysfunction originating in that tissue, organ, or cell type drives loss of function, increased disease risk, and reduced healthspan/lifespan in the whole organism (for example, as could be measured by tissue-specific genetic or pharmacological interventions that delay or accelerate ageing phenotypes systemically).

Identify and rank the tissues, organs, and cell types whose age-related dysfunction makes the largest causal contribution to organismal ageing in mammals. In particular, determine whether ageing is driven predominantly by a small number of "pacemaker" tissues or cell types (and if so, which ones), or whether contributions are broadly distributed across the organism.
artifact.status_search_result: This is a biological open question highlighted as part of a roadmap of unresolved problems in biogerontology. Recent reviews (e.g., on hallmarks of ageing, senescent-cell biology, and tissue-specific ageing clocks) discuss candidate tissues such as the immune system, hypothalamus, vasculature, adipose tissue, and stem-cell compartments, but no consensus ranking has been established. The question remains open.

status_evidence.title: Hallmarks of aging: An expanding universe
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses multiple cellular and tissue-level hallmarks contributing to ageing without identifying a single dominant tissue.
status_evidence.claim: No consensus on which tissues or cell types contribute most to ageing.

status_evidence.title: Cellular senescence: defining a path forward
status_evidence.snippet: Reviews tissue-specific roles of senescent cells in driving systemic ageing, noting open questions about relative contributions.
status_evidence.claim: Relative tissue contributions to ageing are still under active investigation.
